newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour, Alliance to resume talks in evening.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour, Alliance to resume talks in evening.

text.p: Leaders of New Zealand's Labour Party and the left-wing Alliance said they would resume their talks on Monday evening at 7.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) on the conditions for Alliance support for a proposed Labour-NZ First coalition.
Labour leader Helen Clark left to meet New Zealand First leader Winston Peters and was taking information from the Alliance meeting to discuss with him, a Labour spokesman said.
Asked if he was concerned that progress was slow, Labour deputy leader Michael Cullen told reporters: "I'm not concerned at all, I think we're proceeding in a very good fashion."
He expressed the hope of reaching an agreement with the Alliance negotiating team later in the evening.

A Labour-NZ First coalition would need support from the Alliance on issues of confidence and money supply. NZ First is expected to decide on Tuesday if it will form a coalition with Labour or the caretaker National Party government.
Any agreement between Labour and Alliance negotiators would also need to be approved by the Alliance council and parliamentary caucus.
Alliance leader Jim Anderton said he had seen as much information as he needed on the policy aspect of a coalition.
"The other side is the confidence issue, which we're also going through in a positive way with Labour," Anderton said.
